modern: With regard to what happens in keeping with nature, we ought to blame neither the gods, for they do nothing wrong either willingly or unwillingly, nor men, for they do nothing wrong except unwillingly. So we should blame nobody.
original: With respect to that which happens conformably to nature, we ought to blame neither gods, for they do nothing wrong either voluntarily or involuntarily, nor men, for they do nothing wrong except involuntarily. Consequently we should blame nobody.

explained.summary: There’s no one to blame for what happens in the natural course of things. Not the gods, who never do wrong, and not people, who only do wrong out of ignorance rather than real intent. Blame has no proper target, so let it go.
explained.today: When a holiday is ruined by storms, there’s nothing to rage at. When a flatmate leaves the kitchen in a state, they’re probably not plotting against you, just careless or unaware. Dropping the urge to find a culprit saves a lot of energy.
